newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada lumber companies to get export quotas today.
newsitem.headline: Canada lumber companies to get export quotas today.

text.p: Canadian lumber companies will receive their quarterly allocations for softwood lumber shipments to the United States on Thursday, but a spokeswoman for the International Trade department said the quota information will be confidential.
Nicole Bourget, director of communications for International Trade Minister Art Eggleton, said it would be up to the companies to reveal what their export limits are.
"They can release it if they want to, but by law we cannot reveal it," Bourget said. She said letters to the companies would be sent in the early afternoon.

Under an agreement between Canada and the United States that took effect on April 1, Canadian lumber shipments that exceed 14.7 billion board feet annually, or 4.226 billion board feet quarterly, are subject to export fees.

During the first two quarters of the agreement, export permits were processed on a first-come, first-served basis, but starting with the third quarter, which began on October 1, export permits are issued according to individual export quotas for very lumber exporting company.

Under the new allocation, lumber exporters based in British Columbia will get 59 percent of the total annual quota, Quebec companies will get 23 percent, Ontario companies 10.3 percent and Alberta exporters 7.7 percent.
The new allocation goes to primary producers and remanufacturers who process lumber further, while wholesalers of lumber are not given direct quotas.
The allocation will be reviewed annually for the next four years of the life of the Canada-U.S. agreement.
-- Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
